evidence: MITRE CVE record (published 2025-08-05), title 'Cursor Agent is vulnerable to prompt injection via MCP Special Files': '...if sensitive MCP files, such as the .cursor/mcp.json file don't already exist ... an attacker can chain a indirect prompt injection ... trigger RCE on the victim without user approval.' Fixed in 1.3.9.
correction: Add the precondition: affects Cursor < 1.3.9 and only when .cursor/mcp.json does not already exist (creating a new dotfile needed no approval).

evidence: MITRE CVE record (2025-08-05): 'In versions below 0.2.111, a path validation flaw using prefix matching instead of canonical path comparison, makes it possible to bypass directory restrictions and access files outside the CWD.'
correction: Optionally specify: Claude Code < 0.2.111; exploitation needs a same-prefix directory and untrusted content in the context window.

evidence: Pillar Security blog, 18 Mar 2025 (Ziv Karliner et al.): payload 'undetectable to human reviewers but fully readable by AI models'; hidden Unicode 'appear invisible on the GitHub platform pull request approval process'. Vendor responses: Cursor called it user responsibility; GitHub added hidden-Unicode warning 1 May 2025.
correction: Exact wording of the 'unwitting accomplice' quote [verify] (fetch confirmed the phrase 'an unwitting accomplice'; full sentence not re-checked verbatim).

evidence: Aikido blog 'PromptPwnd: Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in GitHub Actions Using AI Agents', Rein Daelman, 4 Dec 2025: 'Live proof-of-concept exploits already exist, and several major open-source projects are affected.' Gemini CLI case: agent wrote API keys/tokens into an issue body.
correction: Phrase as 'can leak secrets' (shown via PoC, e.g. Gemini CLI workflow), not that all such agents leak.

evidence: Invariant Labs, 'MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks', 2025-04-01 (Beurer-Kellner, Fischer). Mitigations, Tool and Package Pinning: 'Clients should pin the version of the MCP server and its tools to prevent unauthorized changes... using a hash or checksum'.

arXiv 2508.14925 (Wang, Gao, Wang, Liu, Sun, Cheng, Shi, Du, Li; v1 19 Aug 2025): '45 live, real-world MCP servers and 353 authentic tools'; 'with o1-mini, achieving an attack success rate of 72.8%'; 'highest refused rate (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) less than 3%'.
correction: Refusal <3% is the highest refusal rate across evaluated agents (Claude-3.7-Sonnet), not o1-mini's specifically; 72.8% is the top ASR (o1-mini). A v2 exists (dated 29 Sep 2026) [verify numbers unchanged].

evidence: arXiv 2402.07867 (Zou, Geng, Wang, Jia; v1 Feb 2024, v3 Aug 2024; 'To appear in USENIX Security Symposium 2025'): 'PoisonedRAG could achieve a 90% attack success rate when injecting five malicious texts for each target question'.
correction: Five poisoned texts per target question (into a knowledge database with millions of texts) yield 90% ASR. Year: arXiv 2024, venue USENIX Security 2025.

evidence: MITRE CVE record (2024-03-29), 'Xz: malicious code in distributed source': 'the liblzma build process extracts a prebuilt object file from a disguised test file existing in the source code' (xz 5.6.0+ upstream tarballs).
